Women in whom maternal HAART is not indicated, or those living in countries where HAART is not available, should be given short-course zi- dovudine starting at 28 weeks of pregnancy or as soon as feasible thereafter and continued into labour. A single dose of nevirapine should be given at the onset of labour to the mother followed by 7 days treatment with zidovudine and lamivudine to reduce the emergence of nevirapine resist- ance. Infants born to these mothers should be given zido- vudine for 7 days from birth and a single dose of nevirap- ine within 72 hours of birth. Women presenting late in pregnancy and who have not received HAART or com- pleted at least 4 weeks of zidovudine may be given one of the following regimens: • a single dose of oral nevirapine plus oral zidovudine and lamivudine during delivery followed by 7 days postpar- tum treatment with oral zidovudine and lamivudine; the newborn should be given a single oral dose of nevirap- ine plus oral zidovudine for 4 weeks • oral zidovudine and lamivudine during delivery, fol- lowed by 7 days postpartum treatment with oral zidovu- dine and lamivudine; the newborn should also get 7 days treatment with oral zidovudine and lamivudine • a single dose of oral nevirapine at the onset of labour; the newborn should also have a single oral dose of nev- irapine. Infants born within 2 hours of the mother taking a single oral dose of nevirapine or to mothers who have taken less than 4 weeks of antiretroviral prophylaxis (or none at all), should be given a single dose of oral nevirapine immedi- ately after birth plus 4 weeks of oral zidovudine. Other measures necessary to minimise the transmission of infection include the rigorous selection of blood donors, microbiological screening of blood, and, where possible, heat treatment of blood products. Maternal vitamin A de- ficiency has been identified as a risk factor for vertical transmission in Africa (see p.1974). Nutritional interven- tion and vaginal cleansing during labour could reduce ver- tical transmission in regions where zidovudine therapy is not readily available. 1. CDC.
